newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Drugs crimes up sharply in Moscow in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Drugs crimes up sharply in Moscow in 1996.

text.p: Drug-related crimes rose sharply in Moscow in 1996, despite a slight drop in crime overall in the Russian capital, Interfax news agency said on Thursday
The agency quoted the Moscow branch of the Russian interior ministry as saying more than 4,600 crimes involving drugs were registered last year in the capital, compared with just over 3,000 in 1995.

It gave no reason for the 65 percent rise but it appeared to reflect a trend. Preliminary interior ministry figures last month showed a rise in drug-related crimes for all Russia, which drug traffickers cross on the way from Central Asia to Europe.
Interfax said the number of all registered crimes in Moscow had fallen to just over 87,600 in 1996 from more than 92,600 in 1995.
It said the number of crimes described as "banditry" and "terrorism" had fallen, as had the number of premeditated murders.
Crime remains a major problem in Moscow and the rest of Russia, particularly with the rise of criminal gangs since the Soviet Union broke up in 1991.

Crimes in Moscow last year included separate bomb blasts which killed 13 people at a cemetery and four at an underground rail station, explosions which wounded more than 30 people on two trolleybuses, and the murder of a U.S. businessman.
President Boris Yeltsin said in November crime must be tackled urgently and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has said the level of crime is so high that Russia's state security is threatened.
